title: Review of c02's FCH chemoton (SIBE) on fresh seed 13 with its starved fork: a K-ringed vesicle forms from noise and holds its size, but a K-free ring beside it does too, and 300 time units after the feed cut both have shrunk without dying
summary: Fresh seed 13 of world.py and world_starve.py (feed cut at t=300, identical until then), 192^2, T=600. From noise, a double-walled vesicle forms by t~150 whose outer bilayer carries a closed ring of catalyst K (labkit K rim/core 6.5, rim/outside 1.9; fork_s13.png row 2), and it holds its amphiphile mass at 1393 -> 1392 from t=300 to 600. A second, K-free ring in the corner (K 0.3 against 1640 in the vesicle) also holds its mass (about 1000 -> 990) in the fed run, so on this seed persistence does not require the individual's own catalyst: amphiphile reaches it through the bath. After the feed cut, total amphiphile falls 2489 -> 352 and K 2320 -> 258 (K collapses from the ring into two beads), the K vesicle loses its outer bilayer and shrinks from mass 2005 to 524, and the K-free ring shrinks from about 1000 to 480; both are still intact rings at t=600 (bodies_s13.txt). I see S, I and the K layer (B); the fork shows starvation shrinks individuals, but none dies within the run, and the fed twin shows a catalyst-free body maintained by its neighbour's product, so E is not seen at the individual level.

observations.S: rerun/seed13/sheet.png t=0: uniform noise in every channel; vesicles by t~150
observations.I: bodies_s13.txt: the K vesicle at (73,100) keeps mass 1393-1397 and area 1150-1166 from t=297 to 600; rerun/seed13/sheet.png
observations.B: fork_s13.png row 2 (fed, K channel): a closed K ring on the vesicle's outer bilayer at t=297-600; labkit radial K rim/core 6.53, rim/outside 1.91 (rerun/seed13/FACTS.md, track 19 membrane-like in u and K)

seeds_run.result: partial: S, I and the K layer reproduce on one K vesicle; a K-free ring persists alongside it; the starved fork shrinks both individuals (mass -74% and -52% by t=600) but neither dies

controls_run.E: starve/seed13 (world_starve.py, feed cut at t=300) against rerun/seed13 (fed twin, identical until t=300): bodies_s13.txt, fork_s13.png

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The L4c gate asks for individuals that die at the fork; on seed 13 the starved vesicle and ring are still intact at t=600 (300 after the cut), only smaller, so I cannot call the death part, and a longer fork would settle it. In the fed run a ring without catalyst persists at constant size beside the K vesicle, so maintenance is shared through the bath rather than owned by each individual (as the claim's own seed-1 note says). The K layer is placed on the bilayer by the designed gate, and its ablation (no gate) removes everything, not just the layer; I did not re-run those controls.
